text: Agribank, HDBank lead banking and financial services category in VARI 2026 rankings

HCM CITY - Agribank and HDBank ranked first and second, respectively, in the banking and financial services category of the 2026 Ranking of Enterprises for Sustainable Agricultural Development, recognising their contributions to providing capital and financial services to the agricultural and rural sectors.
The results were announced at a ceremony in Hà Nội on November 18.

The ranking is part of the Vietnam Agriculture Reputation Index (VARI) programme, organised by the Centre for Trade Promotion and Human Resource Development under the Vietnam General Association of Agriculture and Rural Development.

The ranking was based on an assessment combining corporate profiles, market surveys and expert opinions, using key criteria including financial capacity, market reputation, technological innovation, contributions to the agricultural sector, sustainable development and corporate governance.
This year's banking and financial services category featured five institutions.
Following Agribank and HDBank, BIDV, Sacombank and VietinBank took the third, fourth and fifth positions, respectively.

Through credit, payment services, trade finance and connections across agricultural value chains, banks help meet financial needs from production to consumption, supporting businesses, cooperatives and farmers in developing their operations.

Ranked second in the category, HDBank was recognised for developing tailored financial solutions for agricultural and seafood exporters, as well as end-to-end distribution supply chains to serve all stakeholders within a closed-loop ecosystem.

By focusing on key touchpoints and value creation, the bank has progressively rolled out digital support solutions targeting household businesses and end producers to maximise value for all participants.

These initiatives align with HDBank's orientation on supporting rural areas and second-class cities, meeting their financing needs and helping connect raw material production areas with processing, distribution and consumption activities.

At the event, Trần Hoài Phương, Director of Corporate Banking at HDBank, joined a panel discussion with representatives of agricultural businesses to discuss investment needs, production development and solutions to enhance the value of Vietnamese agricultural products.
Drawing on years of working alongside businesses and rural communities, HDBank has developed financial solutions covering production, distribution and exports.
The bank tailors its financing to borrowers' business plans and cash flow capacity, addressing investment needs ranging from crop cultivation and livestock farming to processing and consumption.
HDBank has introduced a banking model dedicated to agriculture and rural development, alongside value chain financing solutions.

These initiatives expand access to capital for stakeholders ranging from lead businesses to suppliers, farming households and distributors, connecting production, procurement and consumption activities.
The bank has also rolled out dedicated financing programmes to bring capital closer to businesses and producers.
These include a VNĐ4 trillion (US$155.3 million) preferential lending programme for the agriculture, forestry and fisheries sectors, supporting production, processing, exports and market expansion.

HDBank has also partnered in implementing funding from the World Bank-financed Rural Finance and Vietnam Sustainable Agriculture Transformation projects, with an initial limit of VNĐ500 billion ($19.4 million), targeting individuals, farming households and small businesses.
The bank disbursed more than VNĐ42 trillion in green credit between 2019 and 2025.

The completion of its $100 million international green bond programme, with the participation of the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank FMO and British International Investment (BII), underscores its commitment to green growth and supports businesses in investing in technology and using resources more efficiently.
The recognition in the 2026 ranking reflects HDBank's ongoing efforts to support agricultural and rural economic development.

By combining green financing, supply chain finance and digital banking services, the bank helps bring financial solutions closer to businesses and producers, contributing to improved business efficiency and the development of agricultural value chains. - VNS
